rv.q: In a show all about uncertainty, one thing is certain: in Only Human , Brown is at his astounding best.
This is a hugely entertaining, and often joyous, journey into humanity’s ceaseless proclivity for self-deception.
Act two raises the bar... into a stratosphere of one gasp-inducing stunt after another.
It’s a thoroughly entertaining, at times mind-warping exploration of how magical we still find the idea of being able to predict the future, five centuries after Nostradamus.
So, even when he is not at the top of his game, Brown is a formidable entertainer, blending pop psychology, nimble storytelling and an instinctive ability to bond with his audience.

Only Human is a show built on contrasts, intimate yet enormous in scale, playful yet quietly profound, and Brown’s command of the material throughout makes it easy to understand why audiences keep returning for more.
Brown is a master of his craft and Only Human reminds us that he really is one of the greatest showmen of them all.
Smart, unsettling, and wildly entertaining, this is theatre at its most compelling.
For that alone, he deserves our respect and applause.
In this brand-new production, Derren Brown combines mind-reading, psychological illusion, and breathtaking storytelling in a way that is both deeply personal and utterly electrifying.
The chief reveal is that Derren Brown may be past his peak.
Brown's remarkable stage presence, combined with the suspense and uncertainty woven throughout the show, creates an evening that is as thought-provoking as it is entertaining.
Appropriately enough, the result is theatre magic at its finest.
Only Human is an electrifying piece of theatre on the comedy and curiosity within our contradictions.
His latest venture did everything but disappoint.
This is a slick, fast-paced spectacle that will have you slack-jawed throughout.
Brown once again demonstrates why he remains in a league of his own.
If you are all about the SHOCK factor and like a bit of illusion, then this is the show for you!
The answer, it turns out, is with remarkable ease.

Only Human may not present a radical new chapter in his craft, but its real interest lies elsewhere: in prompting us to question how our choices are formed and how our assumptions can help, or hinder, us in living with intention.
Yet while the individual tricks may intrigue, what’s noticeably absent is the storytelling that has often bound his previous shows together.
Derren Brown really is one of a kind, and Only Human is no exception.
Only Human does not just celebrate Derren's commanding stage presence, it also masters elegance in lighting, illusion, and staging.
The show is nothing short of spellbindingly electrifying, with shock after shock.
Brown is a once-in-a-generation talent. He's very funny too, with quick-witted and silly humour. He's a genius.
Brown commands the entire room, and all of the people in it.
Ultimately, this illusionist act is nothing but a big disillusionment.

Ultimately this is little more than music-hall entertainment for the 21st century, where much like the real-life P.T.Barnum or L. Frank Baum's fictional Wizard of Oz, Derren Brown is selling illusion and flim-flam.

cn.t: Brown's latest West End show mostly dazzles with his masterful mentalism and mind-bending illusions, though some critics find it overextended or lacking originality. His commanding stage presence and exploration of free will captivate audiences.
